newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rises slightly on corporate selling of dlr.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rises slightly on corporate selling of dlr.

text.p: The ringgit rose slightly against the dollar in late Asian trading on corporate selling of the dollar, dealers said.

"Ringgit was holding at about 2.5080 (a dollar) for most of the day before the selling," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. He said he heard a big foreign bank was behind the selling which took the ringgit to 2.5060.
Trading was generally thin due to lack of fresh domestic leads and slow moves in the dollar/majors with Tokyo and London on holiday, dealers said.
Dealers said they expected immediate support for dollar/ringgit at 2.5050.
"The ringgit is likely to be capped at 2.5000 as corporate players are expected to buy back the dollar on dips," said a dealer with a foreign bank in Kuala Lumpur.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5060/65 a dollar against 2.5080/90 at the Kuala Lumpur close on Friday.
